DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>: Each group defines one router job. All fields except the two password paths and two device-key paths are required strings. Paths expand ~; relative paths resolve from the working directory. Outputs must be distinct and non-overlapping. Existing outputs may be replaced. Run All validates, decodes, saves, extracts, edits and encodes. HG659 now supports the same existing decode/view/edit/encode and Run All actions using specification-driven XML processing and signed backups.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.model_specs_path: Required router model specification JSON. It contains exactly router_specs and config_fields. router_specs holds identity, shared codec settings, optional encode additions and optional edit settings. Unused properties and empty sections are omitted. Wrapper/checksum/trailer settings are shared because decode validates what encode writes. HG659 uses codec.encryption_settings, codec.signature and encode.private_exponent_hex; protected-field settings are in edit.field_encryption. config_fields is an expandable name/path list; the configuration path belongs in edit.configuration_file. One ROUTER_FUNCTIONS dictionary maps methods directly to portable functions. The loader receives both specification and schema paths. Existing decode/view/edit/encode and combined actions remain available, including migration in TestingTools and file-driven details in AutomationTools. UltraHub cryptographic processing remains unestablished, and local round trips do not prove physical-router restore acceptance.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.template_config_path: Required. Original encrypted router backup; never modified.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.template_router_password_path: Optional configuration field. Text password-file path required at operation time only when the model specification requires a password. AutomationTools does not prompt; a missing required password produces an error. HG659 uses specification-defined fixed keys and requires no password or device-key path.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.target_router_password_path: Optional configuration field. Target password-file path required at operation time only when the model specification requires a password; no interactive fallback.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.router_details_path: Required. JSON object of settings to apply. Keys must match config_fields name values in the model specification. Unspecified settings are preserved. HG659 XML editing uses this same file-driven replacement flow, displays current decrypted values and actual change summaries, encrypts configured protected fields and preserves unrelated bytes. Omitted fields are retained. Standalone Decode/View do not require this file.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.router_details_readme_path: Required. Documentation explaining router details JSON settings and how to add new configuration fields.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.decoded_config_archive_path: Required output path: decoded .tar.gz for TAR/GZIP configurations, or .xml for single-file XML configurations. HG659 XML bytes are preserved, even when strict XML parsing fails. Existing outputs may be replaced; paths must be distinct and non-overlapping.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.decoded_config_path: Required. Required output: directory for extracted configuration files. Existing outputs may be replaced; paths must remain distinct and non-overlapping.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.edited_config_path: Required. Required output: directory for the edited copy. Existing outputs may be replaced; paths must remain distinct and non-overlapping.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.encoded_config_path: Required. Required output: encrypted CFG file for the target router. Existing outputs may be replaced; paths must remain distinct and non-overlapping. HG659 writes a binary .conf after RSA/MD5 signing, zlib compression, zero padding and fixed-key AES encryption. The staged backup must decode to the exact edited XML before publication. No physical router restore is attempted; a local round trip does not prove restore acceptance.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.template_device_key_path: Optional configuration field. Binary template device-key file path required when using device-key derivation. The file must exist and be non-empty. An export password is not a device key; THENC derivation, authentication and signing remain unavailable.
DESCRIPTION.<GROUP>.target_device_key_path: Optional configuration field. Binary target device-key file path required when using device-key derivation. The file must exist and be non-empty. An export password is not a device key; THENC derivation, authentication and signing remain unavailable.
